answer: Require every agent identity to be bonded by a non-refundable stake that vests slowly, like pigment settling out of an ocean of applicants: a new agent's work is only trusted once its stake has aged through several epochs and its peers have attested its output. A Sybil attacker must fund each fake identity with real capital that stays locked, so creating a thousand identities costs a thousand stakes — an expense no jade-grade forgery can fake cheaply, while honest agents earn their bond back through attested work.
